ei.title: The Need to Suppress Persistent Old Theories in Conceptual Learning

fullPassage: How do children learn new concepts? The traditional view of conceptual change was that new learned theories replace old ones: once a child learns that the Earth rotates around the sun, their previous theory, based on their experience of seeing the sun move, that the sun rotates around the Earth, would be overwritten. Recent evidence from adults suggests something more surprising: that these old, incorrect theories remain stored in the brain; often we still need them to drive our perceptual expectations such as where to look for the sun in the sky. But in an educational context, we need inhibitory control to suppress them in order to reach the newer, correct theories. The naive incorrect theory is more familiar and automatic; the new theory needs time and deliberate suppression of the old theory to be actively retrieved.

questions.passage: How do children learn new concepts? The traditional view of conceptual change was that new learned theories (A)[replace / reinforce] old ones: once a child learns that the Earth rotates around the sun, their previous theory, based on their experience of seeing the sun move, that the sun rotates around the Earth, would be overwritten. Recent evidence from adults suggests something more surprising: that these old, incorrect theories remain stored in the brain; often we still need them to drive our perceptual expectations such as where to look for the sun in the sky. But in an educational context, we need (B)[inhibitory / encouraging] control to suppress them in order to reach the newer, correct theories. The naive incorrect theory is more familiar and (C)[automatic / deliberate]; the new theory needs time and deliberate suppression of the old theory to be actively retrieved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② replace - inhibitory - automatic: 새 이론이 옛 이론을 '대체'하고, '억제적' 통제가 필요하며, 옛 이론은 '자동적'이라는 본문 내용.
❌ ① reinforce - inhibitory - automatic: '강화한다'는 대체와 정반대.
❌ ③ replace - encouraging - automatic: '격려하는' 통제는 억제와 정반대.
❌ ④ replace - inhibitory - deliberate: '의도적인'은 새 이론의 특성이지 옛 이론의 특성이 아님.
det.tip: replace(대체하다) ↔ reinforce(강화하다). inhibitory(억제적) ↔ encouraging(격려하는).

questions.passage: How do children learn new concepts? The traditional view of conceptual change was that new learned theories replace old ones: once a child learns that the Earth rotates around the sun, their previous theory, based on their experience of seeing the sun move, that the sun rotates around the Earth, would be (A)[overwritten / preserved]. Recent evidence from adults suggests something more (B)[surprising / predictable]: that these old, incorrect theories remain stored in the brain; often we still need them to drive our perceptual expectations such as where to look for the sun in the sky. But in an educational context, we need inhibitory control to suppress them in order to reach the newer, (C)[correct / outdated] theories. The naive incorrect theory is more familiar and automatic; the new theory needs time and deliberate suppression of the old theory to be actively retrieved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① overwritten - surprising - correct: 이전 이론이 '덮어쓰인다'는 전통적 견해, 뇌에 남아있다는 '놀라운' 증거, '올바른' 이론에 도달하기 위한 억제.
❌ ② preserved - surprising - correct: '보존된다'는 overwritten(덮어쓰기)과 반대.
❌ ③ overwritten - predictable - correct: '예측 가능한'은 surprising과 반대.
❌ ④ overwritten - surprising - outdated: '시대에 뒤진'은 newer, correct와 모순.
det.tip: overwrite(덮어쓰다) ↔ preserve(보존하다). surprising(놀라운) ↔ predictable(예측 가능한).

questions.passage: How do children learn new concepts? The traditional view of conceptual change was that new learned theories replace old ones: once a child learns that the Earth rotates around the sun, their previous theory, based on their (A)[experience / imagination] of seeing the sun move, that the sun rotates around the Earth, would be overwritten. Recent evidence from adults suggests something more surprising: that these old, incorrect theories remain (B)[stored / deleted] in the brain; often we still need them to drive our perceptual expectations such as where to look for the sun in the sky. But in an educational context, we need inhibitory control to (C)[suppress / amplify] them in order to reach the newer, correct theories. The naive incorrect theory is more familiar and automatic; the new theory needs time and deliberate suppression of the old theory to be actively retrieved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ experience - stored - suppress: 태양이 움직이는 것을 본 '경험'에 기반, 옛 이론이 뇌에 '저장'되어 있으며, 올바른 이론에 도달하려면 '억제'해야 한다.
❌ ① imagination - stored - suppress: '상상'이 아닌 실제 관찰 경험.
❌ ② experience - deleted - suppress: '삭제된다'는 remain stored와 정반대.
❌ ④ experience - stored - amplify: '증폭한다'는 억제와 정반대.
det.tip: experience(경험) ↔ imagination(상상). stored(저장된) ↔ deleted(삭제된). suppress(억제) ↔ amplify(증폭).

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① overwritten: 이전 이론이 '덮어쓰인다' — 원문 그대로.
✅ ② disappear: 원문은 remain(남아있다). 오래된 이론이 '사라진다'는 것은 뇌에 저장되어 있다는 본문 핵심과 정반대.
❌ ③ correct: 올바른 이론 — 원문 그대로.
❌ ④ automatic: 자동적인 — 원문 그대로.
det.tip: remain(남아있다) ↔ disappear(사라지다). 핵심: 옛 이론은 사라지지 않고 뇌에 남아있다.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① perceptual: 지각적 기대 — 원문 그대로.
❌ ② suppress: 억제하다 — 원문 그대로.
✅ ③ unfamiliar: 원문은 familiar(익숙한). 잘못된 옛 이론이 '익숙하지 않다'는 것은 more familiar and automatic이라는 본문과 정반대.
❌ ④ deliberate: 의도적인 억제 — 원문 그대로.
det.tip: familiar(익숙한) ↔ unfamiliar(익숙하지 않은). 옛 이론은 더 '익숙하고 자동적'이다.

det.analysis:
✅ ④ restrain: '억제하다, 자제시키다'로 suppress와 동의어.

det.analysis:
✅ ④ sophisticated: '정교한, 세련된'으로 naive의 반의어.

questions.passage:
(A) Recent evidence from adults suggests something more surprising: that these old, incorrect theories remain stored in the brain; often we still need them to <u>drive</u> our perceptual expectations such as where to look for the sun in the sky.

(B) The word <u>drive</u> can also mean something quite different in another context.
questions.stem: 밑줄 없이 제시된 (A)와 (B)의 drive의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 작동시키다 - (B) 운전하다: (A)는 지각적 기대를 '작동시키는' 추상적 의미, (B)는 차를 '운전하는' 물리적 의미.
❌ ① (A) 운전하다 - (B) 작동시키다: (A)에서 기대를 운전한다는 것은 부자연스러움.
❌ ② (A) 작동시키다 - (B) 작동시키다: (B)는 물리적 운전.
❌ ④ (A) 운전하다 - (B) 운전하다: (A)는 추상적 의미.
det.tip: drive: 1. 작동시키다(추상) - 기대/변화 등. 2. 운전하다(물리) - 차/트럭 등.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"To put an end to something by force; to prevent something from being expressed or known."

det.analysis:
✅ ② suppress: 강제로 끝내다, 표현을 막다 = 억제하다.
❌ ① express: '표현하다'는 정반대 의미.
❌ ③ reveal: '드러내다'는 막는 것과 반대.
❌ ④ encourage: '격려하다'는 억제와 반대.
det.tip: suppress = 억제하다, 진압하다. 본문 'suppress them in order to reach the newer, correct theories'.

questions.passage: The old theories require __________ (deliberate) suppression for the new theory to emerge.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 의도적인(deliberate) — 형태 변환 불필요, 원형 그대로.

det.tip: deliberate(형용사: 의도적인) → deliberately(부사) → deliberation(명사).

det.tip: concept(개념, 명사) → conceptual(개념적인, 형용사). conceptual change = 개념적 변화.

det.analysis:
✅ ① naive: 초기의 단순한 이론을 뜻하는 '순진한'이 적절. 과학적으로 미숙한 이론.
❌ ② advanced: '발전된'은 incorrect와 모순.
❌ ③ reliable: '신뢰할 수 있는'은 incorrect와 모순.
❌ ④ proven: '증명된'은 incorrect와 모순.
det.tip: naive theory = 순진한/소박한 이론. 경험에 기반한 초기의 단순한 이론.

questions.passage: How do children learn new concepts? The traditional view of conceptual change was that new learned theories replace old ones: once a child learns that the Earth rotates around the sun, their previous theory, based on their experience of seeing the sun move, that the sun rotates around the Earth, would be overwritten. Recent __________ from adults suggests something more surprising: that these old, incorrect theories remain stored in the brain; often we still need them to drive our perceptual expectations such as where to look for the sun in the sky. But in an educational context, we need inhibitory control to suppress them in order to reach the newer, correct theories. The naive incorrect theory is more familiar and automatic; the new theory needs time and deliberate suppression of the old theory to be actively retrieved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ evidence: 성인 대상 최근 '증거'가 놀라운 사실을 시사한다.
❌ ① complaint: '불만'은 연구 맥락과 무관.
❌ ② demand: '요구'는 문맥 부적절.
❌ ③ opinion: '의견'보다 evidence가 과학적 맥락에 적합.
det.tip: evidence(증거) = 연구 결과에 기반한 사실적 근거.
